title: Select Inscriptions Bearing on Indian History and Civilization, Volume I: From the Sixth Century B.C. to the Sixth Century A.D.
note: approved under delegation 2026-09-14: verified by researcher as peer-reviewed or government/university-published. Second edition, revised and enlarged, published by the University of Calcutta, 1965. The standard critical anthology of early Indian inscriptions; Sircar was Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Calcutta University and formerly Government Epigraphist for India. Needed as the second, independent edition of the Hathigumpha inscription (No. 91, pp. 213-221), whose readings and dating differ from Jayaswal & Banerji in Epigraphia Indica XX. Read in the archive.org scan dli.calcutta.11040.

title: Ancient India as Described by Ptolemy
note: approved under delegation 2026-09-14: verified by researcher as peer-reviewed or government/university-published. McCrindle's annotated translation of the Indian chapters of Ptolemy's Geographia, with S. N. Majumdar Sastri's additional notes. Needed as a source distinct from `ptolemy-geographia` because the claims cited (Sambalaka = Sambalpur, the diamond district, V. Ball's objection to the Adamas identifications) are the modern editors' commentary, NOT anything Ptolemy wrote; citing them under Ptolemy would misattribute them. Read in the archive.org scan `in.ernet.dli.2015.65897`, a Today & Tomorrow's Printers and Publishers (New Delhi) reprint edited by Ramchandra Jain, whose pagination matches the 1927 Calcutta edition cited by Patra 2014, n. 6. The reprint's own imprint date is not printed; a reviewer should confirm which edition to name in the bibliography.
